clue.text: Sudden wind, you said, expelled by call for very little cover

indicators.note: by places the ring next to what is left of the wind
expelled tells us to throw these letters out of the gust of wind

parts.note: a gust is a sudden blast of wind
the letter U is spoken just like the word you
to ring someone is to call them on the phone

explanation.surface: A gust of wind blows away someone's request for skimpy clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'you said' is the letter U because it sounds like 'you'; 'expelled' takes it out of GUST to leave GST, and 'by' sets RING beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A G-string is a tiny thong garment, so it gives its wearer almost no covering.

clue.text: Submissive person's hard-core yarn

definitions.meaning: in bondage slang, a submissive partner who is dressed in a full leather suit
a silk or cotton twist thread with a stiff wire or cord running through the middle

explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'person' is a link meaning 'is'. 'Hard-core' looks like a word for extreme, but here it describes yarn that has a stiff core.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses belong to the same short word, one from fetish slang and one from haberdashery trimmings.

clue.text: Superior women lead a salesman into vulgar form of direct marketing

indicators.note: lead works with into: the superior women lead the salesman, all of them going inside the vulgar word
into places the whole string of pieces inside the word for vulgar

parts.note: tarty means cheap and vulgar in style
upper means higher or superior, as in upper class
a rep is a sales representative

explanation.surface: Snooty ladies steer a travelling salesman towards some tacky selling method.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' and 'into' together say the women and salesman are led inside the vulgar word; 'Superior' reads as an adjective on women but supplies its own piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tupperware party is a home gathering where a host sells plastic food boxes to guests, a classic case of selling straight to customers.

clue.text: Fight and kill to begin chiller

indicators.note: to begin says the kill piece is placed at the start, ahead of the fight piece

parts.note: to ice someone is gangster slang for killing them
to box is to fight with the fists

explanation.surface: Brawling and murder are the start of a horror story.
explanation.definitionFit: An icebox is an old-fashioned refrigerator, something that keeps food cold.

clue.text: $1,000 capital won restriction of output

parts.note: a grand is a thousand dollars, abbreviated G
Oslo is the capital city of Norway
W is the abbreviation for won in sports results tables

explanation.surface: A thousand dollars of seed money in a foreign city has curbed production.
explanation.definitionFit: A go-slow is a form of industrial protest in which workers deliberately cut their productivity.

clue.text: I'll contain the fumes Rod L. Johnson initially kept inside

indicators.note: kept inside places the name pieces within the rod

parts.note: a bar is a rod of metal or wood
ell is the spelt-out name of the letter L

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of the surname

explanation.surface: A man called Rod L. Johnson seems to be locked up, perhaps with something noxious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'L.' looks like Johnson's middle initial but is the letter's spelt-out name. Chambers says a bell jar is used to confine gases, so the definition speaks as the jar itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass dome placed over apparatus in a laboratory traps gases, so it speaks of holding vapours in.

clue.text: Brutal bullies in Big Sur

indicators.note: bullies means knocks about, so the letters of the following words are roughed up into a new order

explanation.surface: Thugs throw their weight around on the Californian coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bullies' reads like a noun, but it is a verb telling us to rearrange IN BIG SUR. Big Sur is a stretch of the California coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A bruising encounter is a hard, punishing one, so the word works as a near synonym of harsh.

clue.text: Tough Victorian partiality not complete without accepted rights

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the shortened liking goes round the other pieces
not complete means the final letter of the word for partiality is cut off

parts.note: a liking for something is a partiality towards it
R stands for right, so RR is two rights

explanation.surface: A Victorian-era moralist is less than fully sympathetic towards people's entitlements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, round the inserted pieces; 'not complete' drops the last letter of the partiality word. 'Victorian' means from the Australian state of Victoria, not the British era.
explanation.definitionFit: Larrikin is Australian slang for a rowdy, boisterous young man or hooligan.

clue.text: They joke about Los Angeles Games having no energy — they're really not cool!

indicators.note: about means the jokers go round the other pieces

parts.note: japers are people who jape, that is, play jokes
PE, physical education, is what school games lessons are
taken as written
pep means vigour or energy

explanation.surface: Comedians mock the Los Angeles Olympics for being lifeless, which is hardly cool of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having no energy' looks like a deletion of E, but it is NO plus PEP. PE is physical education, the British school name for games lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: These Mexican chillies are spicy hot, the opposite of cool, so the definition plays on heat rather than fashion.

clue.text: Philosophical scientist understood graduate's trick

parts.note: roger is the radio reply meaning message received and understood
a BA is a Bachelor of Arts graduate
a con is a swindle or trick

explanation.surface: A philosopher catches on to some clever scam pulled by a university leaver.
explanation.definitionFit: The thirteenth-century English friar was an early advocate of experimental science as well as a philosopher.

clue.text: MP squeezed inside tree

indicators.note: squeezed inside says the second letter of the clue's abbreviation is pushed into the first letter's expansion

parts.note: M is short for male, so it is written out in full, and its partner letter P is the piece put inside
M is short for male, so it is written out in full, and its partner letter P is the piece put inside

explanation.surface: A politician gets squashed up among the branches.
explanation.walkthrough: MP is not a politician here: M is expanded to MALE and the P is squeezed into it.
explanation.definitionFit: A maple is a broadleaf tree of the genus Acer, known for its syrup.

clue.text: Boringly traditional supporter's position

parts.note: square is slang for dull and conventional
a leg supports a table or a body

explanation.surface: Some dull, old-fashioned fan holds a fixed view.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'supporter' is a link. In cricket this fielding position is level with the batsman on the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket this is one of the named fielding stations, so it is a place where a player stands.

clue.text: What about feigned sorrow in a fan who's OTT?

indicators.note: about here turns the word round

parts.note: eh is an exclamation asking what

indicators.note: feigned means faked, so the letters of sorrow are put into a false order

parts.note: hip and in both mean fashionable
per means a, as in twice a year

explanation.surface: Someone asks why a wildly over-the-top fan is pretending to grieve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What about' reads as a question but is the reversal; 'in' is not a container signal, it means fashionable; 'a' means per, as in twice a year.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who idolises a celebrity excessively is an overenthusiastic devotee.

clue.text: Slight neck spasm for Spooner that may raise a list of options

definitions.text: that may raise a list of options

indicators.note: for Spooner says the sounds of the two words are swapped in the manner of the Reverend Spooner

parts.note: light means slight or not heavy
a crick is a painful stiffness in the neck

explanation.surface: A mild twinge in the neck, as the muddled Reverend Spooner might put it, brings up a computer menu.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the L and R sounds of LIGHT CRICK gives RIGHT CLICK. Commenters on the blog thought this a loose spoonerism, as the swapped sounds are not both at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Clicking the right-hand mouse button on a computer typically opens a context menu of choices.

clue.text: State's big town, say, not welcoming outsiders

indicators.note: not welcoming outsiders means each word loses its first and last letters, keeping only the middle

explanation.surface: A city in some American state shuts out strangers.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'State' is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Iowa is a farming state in the American Midwest.

clue.text: NUT quit insinuating false identification

indicators.note: quit says the three letters of the union name leave the longer word
false means the remaining letters are given a bogus new order

parts.note: NUT is the National Union of Teachers, a British trade union

explanation.surface: A teachers' union walks away from hinting at a phoney ID badge.
explanation.walkthrough: Take N, U and T out of INSINUATING to leave ISINAING, then rearrange it. The NUT is Britain's National Union of Teachers.
explanation.definitionFit: Insignia are badges or emblems that mark out rank or membership, so they identify the wearer.

clue.text: Check rather round sherry glass

indicators.note: round means the rather word goes around the check

parts.note: sooner means rather, as in I'd sooner stay
CH is the chess abbreviation for check

explanation.surface: Hold back a bit before buying another round of sherry.
explanation.definitionFit: A schooner is a tall drinking glass used in Britain for sherry or port.

clue.text: Get quite down to earth: he has opposite views about Tony Hall's work

indicators.note: about means the two versions of the pronoun sit around the next piece

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: opposite views means the pronoun is also seen from the other side, read backwards

parts.note: Tony Hall became BBC Director-General, DG, in 2013
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A man takes a down-to-earth line opposing the BBC chief's latest project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opposite views' says the pronoun is seen both ways round, forwards and backwards. Tony Hall became Director-General of the BBC in 2013.
explanation.definitionFit: To hedgehop is to fly an aircraft very low, skimming over hedges close to the ground.

clue.text: Hard looking after number one, when fellow out back is a renowned labourer

parts.note: H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

indicators.note: back means the shortened piece is read in reverse
out tells us the fellow leaves the word

parts.note: self-care is looking after oneself, number one

explanation.surface: A tough worker cares only about himself, then sends his mate away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' takes F from SELFCARE to leave SELCARE, and 'back' turns that into ERACLES.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek hero, called Hercules by the Romans, performed twelve famous labours.

clue.text: Partner and antagonist with back-to-back theatre jobs

parts.note: an op is an operation, the work done in an operating theatre

indicators.note: back-to-back means the second copy is placed facing the first, read backwards

parts.note: a second operation, written the other way round

explanation.surface: An opponent and colleague puts on two shows in a row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'theatre' is the operating theatre, not the stage: OP followed by its reversal, PO.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, a person's opposite number can be either a colleague or a rival, which covers both clue words.

clue.text: Great to catch a French composer

indicators.note: to catch means the great word holds the French article

parts.note: good means great or very fine
un is the French word for a

explanation.surface: A great man manages to land a French composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Gounod was the nineteenth-century French composer of the opera Faust.

clue.text: Pub on map exuding a quiet calmness

parts.note: PH, public house, is the abbreviation for a pub on British maps
on is the leg side in cricket

indicators.note: exuding means letting the following pieces seep out of the map

parts.note: P stands for piano, quietly, in music

explanation.surface: A tavern marked on a map gives off a tranquil air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is LEG because the on side is the leg side in cricket; MAP loses A and P to leave M.
explanation.definitionFit: Phlegm in its old sense of temperament means coolness and composure under pressure.

clue.text: A high point for South Africans

definitions.text: A high point for South Africans

parts.words: A high point for South Africans
parts.note: a cape is a point of land and hope is something uplifting, so the phrase is a landmark for South Africans and an encouraging high

explanation.walkthrough: A cape is a headland or point; the cape at the tip of South Africa has hope in its name.
explanation.definitionFit: The rocky headland near Cape Town is a famous point jutting into the sea off southern Africa.

clue.text: Trimming review from a listener

indicators.note: trimming means taking off both ends of the word

parts.note: a notice is a newspaper review of a play or book

explanation.surface: Cutting down a critique that came from a radio listener.
explanation.walkthrough: The ends come off NOTICE, a review of a show or book.
explanation.definitionFit: Otic is a medical adjective meaning relating to the ear, the organ that hears.

clue.text: I smell foul Chinese political all-rounder

parts.note: I smell foul can be put as I am rank, shortened to I'm rank
the Han are the majority ethnic group of China

explanation.surface: Someone admits to stinking, perhaps from a Chinese takeaway.
explanation.walkthrough: Imran Khan was a Pakistani cricket all-rounder who became a politician; all-rounder is a cricket term for a player who both bats and bowls.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pakistani cricketer who batted and bowled later led his country's government.

clue.text: Choose to build, employing the other hand

indicators.note: the other hand swaps left for right, so the L becomes R

parts.note: to elect is to choose by vote

explanation.surface: Picking a builder who works with the opposite hand.
explanation.walkthrough: L and R stand for left and right, the two hands.
explanation.definitionFit: To erect a building or structure is to put it up or construct it.

clue.text: Opener's endless moan gets cameraman

parts.note: a key opens a lock

indicators.note: endless means the moan loses its final letter

parts.note: a gripe is a complaint or moan

explanation.surface: The first batsman's ceaseless whining gets someone with a camera involved.
explanation.walkthrough: A key grip is the chief grip on a film set, who handles the camera mounts and rigging rather than operating the camera.
explanation.definitionFit: On a film crew the chief grip runs the camera rigging and dollies, loosely a camera technician.

clue.text: Death by cocaine may not be to everyone's taste?

definitions.text: may not be to everyone's taste?

indicators.note: by places the drug letter next to the word for death

parts.note: demise means death
C is slang shorthand for cocaine

explanation.surface: Dying from drug use is not something everyone would enjoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Demi-sec is medium-dry wine or champagne, which suits some palates but not others.
